abstract_summary: AI agents now generate biological hypotheses faster than they can be tested. Hypotheses stated at the atomic level can be examined with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. For new questions without a reference, trust in an agent-run simulation rests on a tool-written process record, not the agent's account. Existin...

dence behind a result. MDClaw connects a scientist's hy-
pothesis or prompt to a coding agent that plans simulations,
executes them and analyzes the results (Fig. 1a). The scien-
tist can be a human researcher or an AI system. An expert-
designed harness provides 14 protocol documents, termed
agent skills, and 100 command-line tools spanning structure
preparation through trajectory analysis (Fig.1b). Skills guide
planning, while tools perform the calculations and enforce
technical checks. The agent can select and revise a workflow
while the harness retains its inputs, settings and outputs. The
tools also run enhanced-sampling and alchemical free-energy
methods (Supplementary Fig. 2).

This measures conformity to a defined simulation task, rather
than equilibrium convergence or biological validity.
We ran Kimi-K3, DeepSeek-V4.1-flash, GLM-5.3-flash
and Qwen3.8-27B in the pi coding agent under three con-
ditions: the simulation software container alone, MDClaw
tools, and MDClaw tools plus skills. Each model ran the
same prompt three times per system and condition (Fig. 2d).
The primary metric, pass^3, is the fraction of systems pass-
ing all three runs. The pass@1 metric is the fraction of suc-
cessful individual runs. Development tasks guided improve-
ment, and the test tasks evaluated the pre-optimization and

releases, including container dependencies, and does not iso-

The harness improves repeated success. Without MD-
Claw, 21 of 372 individual runs passed (pass@1 5.6%,
95% Wilson confidence interval 3.7–8.5%). With tools
alone, pass^3 reached 25–29 of 31 systems (81–94%) and
pass@1 reached 90–98% across models (Fig. 3d,e). Adding
skills increased these ranges to 28–31 systems (90–100%)
and 94–100%, respectively. Most of the improvement was
already present with the command-line harness, and skills
added to it. For DeepSeek, GLM and Qwen, MDClaw cut
median token usage by 42–77%, as validated commands re-
placed trial-and-error scripting and model calls fell. Kimi-K3
was the exception, because without MDClaw it submitted its
scripts after few model calls and 84 of 93 such runs failed
(Fig. 3c).

of runs had nothing to grade and no single check failed in
more than 3% of runs.
Removing the DAG reveals process errors in success-
ful runs. To separate the contribution of the DAG, we built
a version of MDClaw without it and evaluated it on the
30 non-membrane test systems with the same four models
and prompts, three runs per system and tools without skills
(Methods). The chemistry code and validating checks were
unchanged. Each tool instead reads files from paths the agent

or production did not start from the output of the preceding
stage, when a structure entering a stage was not the recorded
output of an earlier stage or had changed after it was written,
or when a stage was missing. With the DAG, the same ques-
tions were answered from node parents, node status and the
system hashes recorded by each node. The DAG records do
not hash the starting state of production, which the tool reads
from its parent node. Failure episodes were counted per run
from the transcript and Slurm accounting: an episode begins
at a tool result reporting failure, or at an MD job that did not
complete, and ends when the same stage later succeeds or the
run ends.

missing_information: No reproducible review or selection methodology was detected.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The final evaluation signal is artifact-based grading against held-out deposited MDDB reference simulations, supported by downstream Abl1 substrate studies corroborated by biochemical kinetics and a cyclotide study corroborated by NMR, plus ablation evidence that the DAG prevents process skipping.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Twelve preparation and seven or eight MD checks computed programmatically from agent artifacts against deposited MDDB reference topologies and trajectories on held-out test systems.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Iterative refinement of tools and skills on 128 development tasks, including human specialist review of proposed remedies, without language-model weight changes.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported performance metrics and provenance tracking are solidly grounded in experimental data across synthetic benchmarks and practical biological applications (Abl1 substrate recognition and PNG-1 mutant stability). Claims are carefully bounded regarding the limits of MD sampling, the lack of tamper-proofing if agents retain filesystem write access, and the necessity of independent reference data.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Performance is rigorously evaluated across four open-weight LLMs (3 runs per condition) measuring pass^3 and pass@1 against artifact checks derived from reference simulations, alongside comparisons with baseline simulation containers and MDCrow. A detailed ablation study demonstrates that removing the DAG allows 11 successful artifact runs that masked critical workflow skips (e.g., bypassing minimization or swapping structures), confirming the distinct auditing utility of the graph.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The test benchmark is strictly held-out with sequence-containment filtering, and downstream application studies on Abl1 and PNG-1 validate execution against external biochemical kinetics and NMR literature.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Objective programmatic artifact grading (12 preparation and 7-8 MD checks) against independent deposited MDDB reference simulations on 31 held-out test systems.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Failure diagnoses on 128 development MD tasks reviewed by a human expert to iteratively refine tool checks and skill prompts without changing model weights.

primary.limitations: The authors clearly acknowledge that DAG execution guarantees do not overcome conformational sampling limitations, that the harness cannot autonomously evaluate whether physical force-field choices suit arbitrary scientific problems, and that the DAG requires write-protection to prevent unauthorized modification by agents.
primary.method_assessment: The harness architecture combines 14 protocol skill documents, 100 command-line tools executing standard computational packages (such as OpenMM and AmberTools), and a DAG recording node metadata and enforcing parent-child transition constraints. The benchmark setup leverages 128 development tasks and 31 held-out test tasks curated from MDDB under strict sequence similarity filtering.
primary.quality_rationale: The study provides a thoroughly documented, open-source tool with rigorous methodology and well-controlled evaluations on independent external datasets. The ablation and multi-model experimental design strongly validate the necessity of the proposed harness architecture.
primary.scoped_contribution: The manuscript introduces MDClaw, an auditable harness for coding agents executing molecular dynamics (MD) workflows that enforces stage transitions and provenance using a directed acyclic graph (DAG), alongside MDDataBench, an artifact-based benchmark evaluating MD setup and trajectory properties against deposited MDDB reference simulations.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study provides a thoroughly documented, open-source tool with rigorous methodology and well-controlled evaluations on independent external datasets. The ablation and multi-model experimental design strongly validate the necessity of the proposed harness architecture.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors clearly acknowledge that DAG execution guarantees do not overcome conformational sampling limitations, that the harness cannot autonomously evaluate whether physical force-field choices suit arbitrary scientific problems, and that the DAG requires write-protection to prevent unauthorized modification by agents.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.

research_relevance.value: Directly relevant to autonomous/deep research workflows based on screening evidence.
